from pypdf import PdfReader

 texts.append(f'\\n\\n=== PAGE {i+1} ===\\n\\n'+t)
Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text(''.join(texts))
print(''.join(texts[:3]))

strengths: EA-KD offers a simple, inexpensive modification that uses existing teacher and student outputs, supports both logit and feature distillation, and adds no student inference cost. Figure 1 supports its practical efficiency.
The CIFAR-100 evaluation is extensive: Table 2 reports improvements in 46 of 49 method–architecture combinations, averaging 0.56 percentage points overall and 1.48 points for vanilla KD.

Results support portability beyond CIFAR-100: vanilla KD improves by 3.39 top-1 points on Tiny-ImageNet, and COCO detection improves by 0.81 and 1.68 AP. Transformer-to-CNN and GPT-2 experiments provide additional evidence of applicability.

The weighting equations and presentation are generally clear. Component and temperature ablations, repeated-run evaluations, and training diagnostics strengthen the empirical case. The manuscript appropriately cites its principal datasets, architectures, and distillation frameworks.
weaknesses: The experiments do not isolate sample prioritization from changes in overall distillation strength. The weights in Equations (11)–(14) are not normalized to have mean one, so they also alter the effective KD coefficient throughout training. Moreover, the MLD+LS coefficient changes from 9 to 4. Comparisons against a matched global weighting schedule and equally tuned baseline coefficients are important for attributing gains to the proposed mechanism.

The theoretical motivation overstates what is established. Equations (5)–(7) correctly describe a uniformly initialized student, but a smaller KL divergence for predictions that already match does not establish harmful neglect of informative samples. High predictive entropy can also reflect teacher uncertainty or error. The asserted connection between feature magnitude and low entropy is unsupported, while t-SNE and loss-surface visualizations provide limited evidence for decision-boundary and robustness claims.

The distinctive benefit of student adaptivity remains weakly established. In Table 8, combining teacher and student entropy improves over teacher-only weighting by only 0.07–0.18 percentage points. Although multiple runs are reported, standard deviations or confidence intervals are absent. Given the cited prior work on entropy weighting and sample-wise KD, stronger controlled comparisons are needed to establish the importance of this particular combination.

Important implementation details remain unspecified, especially whether gradients pass through student entropy. Without detachment, the objective introduces an additional entropy-gradient term beyond loss reweighting, changing both implementation and interpretation. Aggregation for detection regions and LLM sequences also needs clarification. Table 8 reports 75.27 for EA-KD versus 75.46 in Tables 2 and 7 without explanation. These reporting issues are individually repairable, but the missing implementation details and central experimental controls leave a slight preference for rejection.
